title: Mice inheriting fear of acetophenone

tellings.quote: well when they were published in in nature there was that the title was inheriting the fear of fathers

plain: Mice taught to fear the smell of a chemical called acetophenone passed that fear on to their offspring, according to a study done at a US university that Rupert Sheldrake, a scientist known for challenging mainstream biology, describes on the show. Sheldrake recalls that when the work was published in the journal Nature, its title was "inheriting the fear of fathers." If it holds, a memory learned in life would pass down to the next generation.
